title: Chelsea: the Touchline Take on the refereeing row
body:
BBC Sport has a refereeing story involving Chelsea and Manchester United [S1]. The headline said it plainly: “Which game will Chelsea's Palmer miss after red card?” [S1]. The names in the frame: Cole Palmer [S1].

For context, BBC Sport also ran: “Chelsea staff warned over Fantasy Premier League use” [S2]. In our Football-Data.co.uk results, Chelsea have 3 wins, 0 draws and 2 defeats from their last 5 league games: 9 points, 9 scored and 4 conceded [ST1]. In our Football-Data.co.uk results, Manchester United have 0 wins, 3 draws and 2 defeats from their last 5 league games: 3 points, 6 scored and 11 conceded [ST2].

One more weekend, one more refereeing row, and still no clarity for supporters. Every row like this sells, but clarity would serve the game far better. The Touchline Take: consistency, please. That is all anyone asks.

evidence.text: BBC Sport: Which game will Chelsea's Palmer miss after red card?. BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains why Cole Palmer's red card suspension will not rule him out of Chelsea's Premier League match against Manchester United.

BBC Sport: Chelsea staff warned over Fantasy Premier League use. Chelsea warn staff to be careful about revealing team news through Fantasy Premier League after Joao Pedro's injury appeared to have been inadvertently disclosed through team selections.
Chelsea last 5 league matches in Football-Data.co.uk results: 3 wins, 0 draws, 2 defeats, 9 points, 9 goals scored, 4 conceded (sequence WWLWL).
Manchester United last 5 league matches in Football-Data.co.uk results: 0 wins, 3 draws, 2 defeats, 3 points, 6 goals scored, 11 conceded (sequence DDLLD).
